newsitem.title: USA: US stock index futures extend opening gain on data.
newsitem.headline: US stock index futures extend opening gain on data.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures opened higher Tuesday on fund buying tied to the new quarter and extended gains on softer than expected manufacturing data, floor traders said.

S&P 500 futures traders said institutional buyers showed up on the first day of the third quarter with funds to invest and predicted the infusion would continue to support futures through the morning.
"People are putting their money to work," one brokerage trader said.

Stock index futures extended their early gains after the National Association of Purchasing Management reported its June business index dipped to 55.7 in June from 57.1 the previous month. Analysts had predicted a smaller decline to 56.4.

Bond futures rallied on the data, which was viewed as a relief following on the heels of a surprisingly strong Chicago regional purchasers index on Monday. The strength in bonds spilled over into index futures, stock traders said.
The September S&P 500 futures contract got as high as 900.75 on the move, just below Monday's high of 901.80.
"Bonds are having a good day, and there's no negative news in sight," said a second brokerage trader on the stock index floor.

However, S&P traders said volume has been light on the upswing, and some doubted there was sufficient momentum to carry the September contract up to a test of Friday's high at 905.00 with many market participants on the sidelines until the conclusion of the two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
The FOMC meets today through Wednesday and is widely expected to leave short-term interest rates unchanged.
Start-of-the-quarter buying could resume after the Fed meetings conclude, stock index futures traders said.
"I think a lot of people will be holding out waiting for the FOMC outcome," the S&P trader said.
Traders pegged support for September S&P 500 futures at 889.25, near today's session low, and at 886.00 and 884.50 below that.
On Thursday, which is a shortened trading session for index futures, U.S. June employment data are set for release. Markets are closed Friday for the July Fourth holiday.
Nonfarm payrolls are forecast to rise 222,000 following May's gain of 138,000. The unemployment rate is predicted unchanged at 4.8 percent.

Sept S&Ps were up 11.75 at 902.00, NYSE New Composites up 5.85 at 471.45, Nikkeis down 315 at 20,280, Midcap 400s up 1.70 at 291.30, Nasdaq 100s up 4.00 at 970.50 and Russell 2000s up 0.75 at 399.65. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
